title: Fresh Food Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The fresh food compartment temperature sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription:
E1 is posted when the fresh food NTC reads open or out of sensible range. The refrigerator falls back to a default duty cycle until the sensor is replaced.

Replacement sensors are inexpensive; most plug in at the top interior panel.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power before accessing the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Snap out the sensor cover and swap the NTC.

faq.a: Yes briefly, but temperatures may drift outside the safe range.

title: Freezer Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer compartment temperature sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates a failed or disconnected freezer NTC. Without this sensor, the control cannot verify that the freezer is at setpoint.

Replacement usually needs access to the rear freezer wall and possibly a brief defrost.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Access rear freezer wall, swap NTC.

whenToCallPro: If access requires full defrost and evaporator removal.

faq.a: Transfer freezer food to another unit until you confirm temperatures are correct.

title: Defrost Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator defrost sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E3 appears when the defrost termination sensor is open or shorted. The control must estimate defrost timing conservatively, which can leave some ice on the evaporator.

Replace the sensor; it is usually clipped to the evaporator tube.

fixSteps.title: Defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 24 hours to clear ice before service.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear freezer panel and replace the defrost sensor.

whenToCallPro: If the harness has heat or ice damage.

faq.a: Repeated freeze-thaw stress on the wire insulation usually causes it.

title: Defrost Heater Fault
shortDescription: The defrost heater did not draw current when energised.
fullDescription:
E4 indicates the defrost heater circuit is open. An open heater element, blown thermal fuse, or open bimetal prevents defrost.

Ice builds up rapidly if not addressed; a defrost now will help but will only be temporary.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure heater, bimetal, and fuse; replace whichever is open.

whenToCallPro: If the defrost harness is routed through foam.

faq.a: Never - it protects against fire from a runaway heater.

title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator fan is not running at target speed.
fullDescription:
E5 is posted when the fan tacho signal is missing or slow. Ice buildup after a defrost failure, a seized motor, or a pinched harness are the usual causes.

Clear ice first, then replace the motor if tacho remains absent.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If E5 persists, swap the evaporator fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If defrost system also needs service.

faq.a: Yes - transfer to another unit during defrost.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Main control and display are not communicating.
fullDescription:
E6 is posted when the UART or I²C link between boards fails. A loose door-hinge harness or a failed board are the usual causes.

Power cycle first; reseat the harness through the top hinge if the fault persists.

faq.a: Usually yes, under a default duty cycle.

title: Damper Motor Fault
shortDescription: The air damper between freezer and fresh food sections is not moving.
fullDescription:
E7 is raised when the damper stepper motor does not report the commanded position. A failed motor, a frozen damper blade, or a broken position switch can cause it.

After a defrost cycle the damper often frees itself; otherwise replace the damper assembly.
symptoms: Fresh food too warm or too cold

fixSteps.title: Replace damper
fixSteps.instruction: If E7 returns, replace the damper assembly.

faq.a: If the damper sticks open, fresh food can freeze.

title: Condenser Fan Fault
shortDescription: The condenser fan is not at target speed.
fullDescription:
E8 indicates the condenser fan tacho is missing or slow. Dust, bent blade, or a failed motor are common causes.

Pull the fridge out, vacuum the condenser, and inspect the fan.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new fan motor if still faulty.

title: Inverter Compressor Fault
shortDescription: The inverter-driven compressor reports a run fault.
fullDescription:
E9 is posted by the inverter board when it cannot start or keep the compressor running. Low supply voltage, locked rotor, or inverter failure are common causes.

Replace the inverter board first; sealed-system service is only needed if the board is fine.

faq.a: Move perishables immediately - E9 usually means no cooling.

title: Ice Maker Fault
shortDescription: The ice maker assembly reports a position or sensor fault.
fullDescription:
E10 appears when the ice maker motor, mould sensor, or fill sensor reports an invalid state. The ice maker is disabled but the rest of the refrigerator continues to operate.

Most repairs are by replacing the entire ice maker module.

fixSteps.title: Check water
fixSteps.instruction: Verify filter is not clogged and water line has flow.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the ice maker assembly if water is fine.

whenToCallPro: If water line leaks or valve needs work.

faq.a: Yes, turn the ice maker off from the control and E10 usually clears.

title: Forced Cool / Fast Freeze Active
shortDescription: The fridge is in quick-cool or fast-freeze mode.
fullDescription:
FF is not a fault - it indicates the fast-freeze or quick-cool boost is active. The compressor runs continuously for several hours then returns to normal cycling.

If FF stays on for more than 24 hours, the mode may be stuck - power cycle to clear it.

fixSteps.title: Disable mode
fixSteps.instruction: Press fast-freeze again to turn it off.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: If FF stays, unplug for 5 minutes.

faq.a: No - it is an active mode indicator.

title: Ambient Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The room ambient temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
RT is posted when the ambient NTC on the main control is failing. This sensor influences defrost timing and compressor duty cycle.

The sensor is on the main board - replacement is usually a board swap.

causes.cause: Failed ambient NTC on main board

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Swap main control if RT persists.

whenToCallPro: Board swap in a high-humidity environment.

faq.a: Yes, the fridge uses default defrost intervals.
